title: Antony commemorated and beyond telling
english: An encomium of the most blessed Hesychius, presbyter of Jerusalem, on our holy father Antony.

The commemoration of the righteous makes the world rejoice. The commemoration of the righteous gives the world light. The commemoration of the righteous makes humanity leap for joy. Everyone who hears rejoices in the commemoration of the righteous. Now Antony is commemorated, and by his commemoration we are all enlightened.

Antony is a citizen of heaven and a teacher of every virtue. In the flesh he imitated those without flesh. He is the lamp of the churches and the trainer of the priests. He is the flower of virginity and the radiance of purity. He is the crown of those in mountains and caves (Hebrews 11:38) and the model of endurance. He is a worker of self-control and an undefeated boxer. He is the pillar of the prophets and the mirror of the apostles. He is strong with God and with people. He holds nothing on earth but looks wholly toward heaven. He lifts his eyes on high and hurries his race toward that prize.

He was faithful as Abraham and obedient as Isaac, enduring as Jacob. Giving grain to Egypt as Joseph, he guided wonders of every kind by his teaching as Moses did. He sang as David did and drove out demons. He offered himself to God as a greater temple. As Daniel did, he gave commands to lions. As John the Baptist does, he gathers the desert into a congregation. As John the Theologian, through meditation on the Gospel he reclines on the breast of Jesus (John 21:20). As Paul does, he died daily (1 Corinthians 15:31).

We too draw, yet the winepress overflows. The jars fill and the vats run over (Joel 3:13 / 4:13 LXX). The more we run, the longer the course becomes. The more the voyage advances, the more the boundlessness of the sea is revealed. Come then, let us also speak the words of Paul: "Time will fail me as I tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David and Samuel and the prophets" (Hebrews 11:32). For Antony, the father of the assembled contests, took all these figures up into himself. Many words are needed, and I serve as a guide to the deeds, since speech grows weary in setting forth the work. The imprint of a shadow is one thing, the working of truth another.
